source_text: ἀχώριστον τῆς θεότητος ὅτι τῷ ἀπροσδεεῖ καὶ παντοδότῃ θεῷ πατρὶ καὶ τῷ υἱῷ αὐτοῦ συνεργεῖ καὶ συμπαρέχει πάντα πᾶσιν, οὐκ εἰς αὔριον ἀναβαλλόμενον, ἅτε δὴ ξύγγνωμον καὶ ὁμόγνωμον πνεῦμα τοῦ πατρὸς, ἀνεκποίητον ἔχον τὸ εἶναι καὶ συμβασιλεύειν αὐτῷ, καὶ τὴν αὐτοῦ, ὅθεν καὶ συνυφεστώτως ἐξῆλθεν, διακληρωσάμενον θεότητα. καὶ ὅτι ὁ παντεξούσιος καὶ πανδύναμος Χριστὸς σὺν τῇ δυνάμει τοῦ αὐτοῦ σεμνοτάτου πνεύματος τὰ σημεῖα καὶ τὰ τέρατα ἐποίησεν καὶ δαίμονας ἐξέβαλεν, ὡς ἐξηγήσαντο οἱ ἱεροφάνται· Μιχαῖας μέν· «τάδε» φησίν, «λέγει κύριος ἐπὶ τοὺς προφήτας τοὺς πλανῶντας τὸν λαόν μου», καὶ μετ' ὀλίγου ἐπιφέρει· «διότι οὐκ ἔσται ὁ εἰσακούων αὐτῶν, ἐὰν μὴ ἐγὼ ἐμπλήσω ἰσχὺν ἐν πνεύματι κυρίου καὶ κρίσεως καὶ δυναστείας.» εἶπεν τοίνυν ποιεῖν ἰσχὺν κύριον ἐν πνεύματι κυρίου, διὰ τὸ καὶ τὴν τριάδα καὶ τὸν σύνδεσμον τῆς φύσεως αὐτῆς δηλῶσαι. αἰνίττεται δὲ τὴν κρίσιν, ἐν ᾗ οὐκέτι λοιπὸν μετάνοια καὶ ὁ εἰσακούων· «ἐν», γάρ, «τῷ ᾅδῃ», φησίν, «τίς ἐξομολογήσεται σοι»; τὸ δὲ «ἐμπλήσω ἰσχὺν» ἀντὶ τοῦ «μεγάλην ἀνταπόδοσιν ποιήσω μετὰ τοῦ θείου πνεύματος». Παῦλος δὲ ὁ δοκιμώτατος ἀποστόλων πρὸς Ἐφεσίους μέν· «τούτου χάριν κάμπτω τὰ γόνατά μου πρὸς τὸν θεὸν πατέρα, ἐξ οὗ πᾶσα πατριὰ ἐν οὐρανοῖς καὶ ἐπὶ γῆς ὀνομάζεται, ἵνα δῷ ὑμῖν κατὰ τὸν πλοῦτον τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ δυνάμει κραταιωθῆναι διὰ τοῦ πνεύ ματος αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸν ἔσω ἄνθρωπον κατοικῆσαι τὸν Χριστόν·» πρὸς Ῥωμαίους δέ· «ἔχω οὖν πεποίθησιν ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ πρὸς τὸν θεόν. οὐ γὰρ τολμῶ τι λαλεῖν, ὧν οὐ κατειργάσατο Χριστὸς δι' ἐμοῦ, λόγῳ καὶ ἔργῳ, εἰς ὑπακοὴν ἐθνῶν ἐν δυνάμει σημείων καὶ τεράτων, ἐν δυνάμει πνεύ ματος ἁγίου.» αἱ ὅμοιαι τῇ φύσει ὑποστάσεις ὁμοίας τιμῆς ἄξιαι· ὅθεν παραπλήσιον καὶ τὸ λόγιον τόδε τῷ· «Χριστὸς θεοῦ δύναμις καὶ θεοῦ σοφία.» Ματθαῖος ἀπὸ τοῦ σωτῆρος· «εἰ δὲ ἐν πνεύματι θεοῦ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια, ἄρα ἔφθασεν ἐφ' ὑμᾶς ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.» καὶ ὡς ἐν τῷ φωτίσματι συμπράττει· ἀδύνατον τοίνυν τῇ συμφωνίᾳ καὶ τῇ ἐνεργείᾳ ὑπάρχειν ἕν, μὴ οὔσης τῆς οὐσίας μιᾶς· καὶ διὰ τοῦτο λέγει ὁ δεσπότης ποτὲ μέν· «ὁ πατὴρ ὁ ἐν ἐμοὶ μένων, αὐτὸς ποιεῖ τὰ ἔργα·» ποτὲ δέ, ὡς νῦν εἴρηται· «ἐγὼ ἐν πνεύματι θεοῦ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια.» διὰ τοῦτο δὲ καὶ Παῦλος εἶπεν· «ἐν δυνάμει πνεύματος ἁγίου», ὁμολογῶν, ὅτι τῇ θείᾳ τῆς τριάδος ἐνεργείᾳ τεθνεῶτας ἤγειραν, αὐτὸς μὲν τὸν Εὔτυχον, Πέτρος δὲ τὴν Ταβήθαν. 7.8ν ὅτι ὥσπερ ὁ θεὸς καὶ πατὴρ, οὕτω καὶ τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα χρηματίζει, σημαινόμενον θεὸς καὶ δεσπότης. ὅτι ὥσπερ ὁ θεὸς καὶ πατήρ, οὕτω καὶ τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα χρηματίζει, σημαινόμενον θεὸς καὶ δεσπότης, καθὰ φράζει Λουκᾶς· «ἦν ἄνθρωπος ἐν Ἰερουσαλήμ, ᾧ ὄνομα Συμεών· καὶ ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος, δίκαιος καὶ εὐλαβής, προσδεχόμενος παράκλησιν τῷ Ἰσραήλ· καὶ πνεῦ μα ἅγιον ἦν ἐπ' αὐτῷ, καὶ ἦν αὐτῷ κεχρηματισμένον ὑπὸ τοῦ πνεύμα τος τοῦ ἁγίου, μὴ ἰδεῖν θάνατον, ἕως ἂν ἴδῃ τὸν Χριστὸν κυρίου. καὶ ἤγετο ἐν τῷ πνεύματι εἰς τὸ ἱερόν. καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ εἰσαγαγεῖν τοὺς γονεῖς τὸ παιδίον Ἰησοῦν τοῦ ποιῆσαι αὐτοὺς κατὰ τὸ εἰθισ μένον τοῦ νόμου περὶ αὐτοῦ· καὶ αὐτὸς ἐδέξατο αὐτὸ εἰς τὰς ἀγκάλας, καὶ εὐλόγησεν τὸν θεὸν καὶ εἶπεν· νῦν ἀπολύεις τὸν δοῦλόν σου, δέσ ποτα, κατὰ τὸ ῥῆμά σου ἐν εἰρήνῃ· ὅτι εἶδον οἱ ὀφθαλμοί μου τὸ σω τήριόν σου.» ἐχρημάτισεν τοίνυν τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα· ἐδέξατο Συμεὼν τὸν Χριστὸν εἰς τὰς ἀγκάλας κατὰ τὸ χρηματισμόν· εὐλόγησεν τὸν χρηματίσαντα, τουτέστιν ἐδόξασεν τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα, ἑορακῶς τὸ σωτήριον τοῦ χρησμοῦ δεξάμενον πέρας· θεόν τε καὶ δεσπότην αὐτὸν τὸν χρηματίσαντα ἐκάλεσεν. ἐχρημάτισεν δὲ ὁ θεὸς πατήρ, τῷ Ἰὼβ φάνας· «οἴει με ἄλλως σοι κεχρηματικέναι, ἢ ἵνα ἀναφανῇς δίκαιος»; οἱ δὲ τῷ ἀληθινῷ πνεύματι τοῦ θεοῦ μάχεσθαι ἠσκηκότες, πανταχοῦ τῆς ὑποθέσεως τὰ ἐν ἄλλοις 74 πράγμασιν καὶ οὐκ εἰς θεολογίαν συντελοῦντα πρὸς τὸ συσκιάσαι τὴν ἀλήθειαν συλλέγοντες καὶ οὐ τὰ πρέποντα τῷ θείῳ μυστηρίῳ ἀτρεκέως ἐκδεχόμενοι καὶ τῇ ὑποθέσει ἁρμόζοντες καὶ πρὸς τὸ κεφάλαιον τοῦτο ἄδεκτα τοῦ θείου προφέρουσιν ῥήματα, ἄνω καὶ κάτω, ὡς μέγα καὶ ἐναργὲς κεφάλαιον, τὸ ψυχρὸν ἐκεῖνο καὶ ἀπατηλὸν ῥῆμα λέγοντες· ὅτι, μησίν, κατάγεται ἐκ τῶν τοιούτων μαρτυριῶν τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα εἰς ἀγγέλου φύσιν, ᾗ καὶ αὐτοὶ φαίνονται χρηματίσαντες. καὶ οὕτως τὰς ὀρθὰς τῶν γραφῶν ἐννοίας ἐξ ἀτόπων ἰδίων λόγων εἰς περιπετείας ἐξέλκουσιν. γέγραπται γάρ, φησίν, ἐν ταῖς ἀποστολικαῖς πράξεσιν· «Κορνήλιος ἑκατοντάρχης,
pass_a_gloss: [Continuing the chapter title from the previous section: ... because of the] inseparable [quality] of the Godhead. That with the God and Father who lacks nothing and gives all, and with his Son, it works together and supplies together all things to all, not putting it off to tomorrow, inasmuch as [it is] the Spirit of the Father sharing knowledge and of one mind, having as inalienable its being and its reigning together with him, and having received by allotment the Godhead of him from whom also, subsisting together, it came forth. And that the all-authoritative and all-powerful Christ, with the power of his own most august Spirit, did the signs and the wonders and cast out demons, as the sacred teachers explained: Micah on the one hand: 'thus,' he says, 'says the Lord concerning the prophets who lead my people astray', and after a little he adds: 'because there will not be the one who hears them, unless I fill strength in the Spirit of the Lord and of judgment and of might.' He said, then, that the Lord makes strength in the Spirit of the Lord, so as to show both the Trinity and the bond of its nature. And he hints at the judgment, in which there is no longer any repentance and the one who hears; 'for in Hades,' he says, 'who will confess to you?' And 'I will fill strength' [stands] for 'I will make a great repayment with the divine Spirit.' And Paul, the most approved of apostles, to the Ephesians: 'For this reason I bend my knees to God [the] Father, from whom every fatherhood in heavens and on earth is named, that he may give you according to the wealth of his glory to be strengthened with power through his Spirit into the inner man, [for] Christ to dwell'; and to the Romans: 'I have then confidence in Christ Jesus toward God. For I do not dare to speak anything of [the things] which Christ did not accomplish through me, by word and work, for obedience of gentiles, in power of signs and wonders, in power of Holy Spirit.' The hypostases alike in nature [are] worthy of like honour; hence this oracle too [is] close to the [one]: 'Christ power of God and wisdom of God.' Matthew from the Saviour: 'but if in the Spirit of God I cast out the demons, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.' And how in the enlightenment it acts together: it is impossible, then, to be one in concord and in operation, the essence not being one; and for this reason the Master says at one time: 'the Father who remains in me, he does the works'; and at another, as has now been said: 'I in the Spirit of God cast out the demons.' And for this reason Paul also said: 'in power of Holy Spirit', confessing that by the divine operation of the Trinity they raised dead [people], he himself Eutychus, and Peter Tabitha. 7.8ν [Chapter title:] That as God and Father, so also the Holy Spirit gives revelations, being signified [as] God and Master. That as God and Father, so also the Holy Spirit gives revelations, being signified [as] God and Master, as Luke declares: 'There was a man in Jerusalem whose name [was] Simeon; and this man, righteous and devout, awaiting consolation for Israel; and Holy Spirit was upon him, and it had been revealed to him by the Holy Spirit not to see death until he should see the Christ of [the] Lord. And he was led in the Spirit into the temple. And it happened, when the parents brought in the child Jesus for them to do according to the custom of the law concerning him, he too received it into the arms, and blessed God and said: now you release your servant, Master, according to your word, in peace; because my eyes saw your salvation.' The Holy Spirit, then, gave the revelation; Simeon received Christ into the arms according to the revelation; he blessed the one who had revealed, that is, he glorified the Holy Spirit, having seen the salvation that had received the end of the oracle; and he called the very one who had revealed both God and Master. And God the Father gave revelation, having declared to Job: 'do you think that I have answered you otherwise than that you might appear righteous?' But those who have practised fighting against the true Spirit of God, everywhere in the subject gathering the things [belonging] to other [page number 74, debris] matters and not contributing to theology, so as to overshadow the truth, and not exactly receiving the things befitting the divine mystery and fitting the subject, bring forward also against this chapter inadmissible sayings of the divine [Scripture], up and down, as a great and evident point, saying that cold and deceitful saying: that, he says [the print has μησίν, read φησίν], from such testimonies the Holy Spirit is brought down into the nature of an angel, by which [nature] they too appear to have given revelations. pass_b_english: He works together with God the Father, who lacks nothing and gives all things, and with his Son, and with them he supplies all things to all, never putting it off until tomorrow. For he is the Spirit of the Father, sharing his knowledge and one with him in mind; his being and his reigning with the Father cannot be taken from him, and he has received as his share the Godhead of the Father, from whom he came forth, subsisting together with him.

And Christ, who holds all authority and all power, did the signs and the wonders and cast out demons with the power of his own most holy Spirit, as the sacred teachers have explained. Micah says: “Thus says the Lord concerning the prophets who lead my people astray” (Micah 3:5); and a little later he adds: “For there will be no one who hears them, unless I fill them with strength in the Spirit of the Lord, and of judgment and of might” (Micah 3:7–8). So he said that the Lord works strength in the Spirit of the Lord, to show both the Trinity and the bond of its nature. And he hints at the judgment, in which there is no longer any repentance, and no one who hears. “For in Hades,” he says, “who will confess you?” (Psalm 6:5). And “I will fill them with strength” stands for “I will make a great requital with the divine Spirit.”

Paul, the most approved of the apostles, writes to the Ephesians: “For this reason I bow my knees to God the Father, from whom every family in heaven and on earth is named, that he may grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened with power through his Spirit in the inner man, so that Christ may dwell in you” (Ephesians 3:14–17); and to the Romans: “I have, then, confidence in Christ Jesus toward God. For I do not dare to speak of anything that Christ has not worked through me, by word and deed, for the obedience of the Gentiles, in the power of signs and wonders, in the power of the Holy Spirit” (Romans 15:17–19). Hypostases alike in nature are worthy of like honour. So this saying too comes close to the words “Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God” (1 Corinthians 1:24). Matthew reports from the Saviour: “But if I cast out the demons by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you” (Matthew 12:28).

And how he works together with them in enlightenment: it is impossible, then, to be one in accord and in working when the essence is not one. And that is why the Master says at one time, “The Father who dwells in me does the works himself” (John 14:10), and at another, as was just said, “I cast out the demons by the Spirit of God” (Matthew 12:28). And that is why Paul too said “in the power of the Holy Spirit” (Romans 15:19), confessing that it was by the divine working of the Trinity that they raised the dead: he himself Eutychus (Acts 20:9–12), and Peter Tabitha (Acts 9:40).
That as God the Father does, so the Holy Spirit too gives revelation, and so is shown to be God and Master.

As God the Father does, so the Holy Spirit too gives revelation, and so is shown to be God and Master, as Luke declares: “There was a man in Jerusalem whose name was Simeon; and this man was righteous and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel; and the Holy Spirit was upon him. And it had been revealed to him by the Holy Spirit that he would not see death before he had seen the Lord’s Christ. And he was led by the Spirit into the temple. And when the parents brought in the child Jesus, to do for him according to the custom of the law, he took him up in his arms, and blessed God and said: ‘Now, Master, you let your servant depart in peace, according to your word; for my eyes have seen your salvation’” (Luke 2:25–30).

So the Holy Spirit gave the revelation. Simeon took Christ into his arms as the revelation had said. He blessed the one who had revealed it, that is, he glorified the Holy Spirit, having seen the salvation that brought the oracle to its fulfilment. And the very one who had revealed it to him he called God and Master. God the Father also gave revelation, when he declared himself to Job: “Do you think I have answered you for any other reason than that you might be shown to be righteous?” (Job 40:8 LXX).

But those who have trained themselves to fight against the true Spirit of God gather from every part of the subject things that belong to other matters and contribute nothing to theology, so as to cast a shadow over the truth. They do not take up precisely what befits the divine mystery and fits the subject, and against this chapter too they bring forward words of Scripture that have no bearing on it. Up and down they repeat, as if it were a great and evident point, that cold and deceitful saying: “From such testimonies,” he says, “the Holy Spirit is brought down to the nature of an angel, since the angels too are seen to give revelation.” And so, out of absurd arguments of their own, they drag the right meanings of Scripture into upheaval. “For it is written,” he says, “in the Acts of the Apostles: ‘Cornelius, a centurion, …

choices.issue: Truncated and garbled draft; text dropped from the middle of 7.7 to the end
choices.choice: 2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-e-u18): retranslated. The old English ended after the second Matthew 12:28 quotation with 'I cast out by the Spirit of God...', then printed 'The text ends abruptly mid-sentence.' and 'bestows an oracle'. Restored: Paul's 'in the power of the Holy Spirit' with Eutychus and Tabitha (end of 7.7), the chapter title 7.8 and its body (Luke 2:25-30, Simeon glorifying the Spirit, Job 40:8), and the opponents' objection leading to Acts 10:22. Fixed: 'Michael says' (Μιχαῖας is Micah), 'co-knowing and co-knowing' (ξύγγνωμον καὶ ὁμόγνωμον), 'all-seeing' (παντεξούσιος, all-authoritative), 'in that abyss' (ᾅδῃ, Hades), 'uncreated being' (ἀνεκποίητον, inalienable). References: (1 Cor 1:24) written in full; (Romans 15:18) widened to Romans 15:17-19; Micah 3:7-8, Psalm 6:5, Acts 20:9-12, Acts 9:40, Luke 2:25-30 and Job 40:8 LXX added. Bracket [it] removed.

choices.why: The end of the chapter title 7.7, which began in the previous section ('because of the …'); only the words this section holds are translated, opened with '…'.
The body opens in outline form with ὅτι, repeating the title; English states it as a sentence.

choices.english: sharing his knowledge and one with him in mind
choices.why: A jingle of two near-synonyms; the old English printed 'co-knowing' twice. συγγνώμων here means sharing knowledge, not 'forgiving'.

choices.term: ἀνεκποίητον ἔχον τὸ εἶναι καὶ συμβασιλεύειν αὐτῷ
choices.english: his being and his reigning with the Father cannot be taken from him
choices.why: ἀνεκποίητος is a legal word for property that cannot be alienated; it is not 'uncreated'.
Didymus' name for the prophets and apostles who expound divine things; 'hierophants' would sound pagan in English.
Micah 3:8 LXX; Didymus reads the 'I' as the Lord, so the object 'them' is supplied from the context of 3:7. KJV reads 'I am full of power', so the reference covers 3:7-8 by Didymus' Greek.

choices.english: so that Christ may dwell in you
choices.why: Didymus' text stops before 'in your hearts by faith'; 'in you' is the plain English object of the infinitive, not an added clause.
Didymus reads πεποίθησιν (confidence) where the usual text of Romans 15:17 has καύχησιν (boast); the English follows his word.

choices.term: καὶ ὡς ἐν τῷ φωτίσματι συμπράττει
choices.english: And how he works together with them in enlightenment:
choices.why: A heading-like phrase in the copy-text; φώτισμα often means baptism, but the Greek does not say so, so 'enlightenment' is kept. 'with them' is the object συμπράττει needs (the Father and the Son).

choices.english: they raised the dead: he himself Eutychus (Acts 20:9–12), and Peter Tabitha (Acts 9:40)
choices.why: Clear references to the two narratives; cited inline.
The chapter turns on χρηματίζω, the word Luke 2:26 uses for the Spirit and Acts 10:22 for the angel; 'reveal' fits both, and 'oracle' renders χρησμός.

choices.english: he was led by the Spirit
choices.why: Didymus' text reads 'was led' where Luke 2:27 has 'came'; the English follows Didymus.

choices.english: when he declared himself to Job
choices.why: φάνας is odd (aorist participle of φαίνω, 'having shown/declared'); the sense is God speaking to Job out of the whirlwind. Job 40:8 is cited with LXX because Didymus quotes the Greek wording ('that you might appear righteous'), which differs from the Hebrew.

choices.english: words of Scripture that have no bearing on it
choices.why: τοῦ θείου (the divine [word]) is rendered 'Scripture'; ἄδεκτος, inadmissible, means here not applicable to the point.
A misprint for φησίν in the copy-text; the English follows φησίν.

choices.english: since the angels too are seen to give revelation
choices.why: αὐτοί refers to the angels implied by 'the nature of an angel'; named in English for clarity.
74 is a printed page number in the copy-text, skipped.
The quotation (Acts 10:22) runs into the next section, where it closes and is cited; only the words this section holds are translated, ending with '…'.
